s1.syndrome_frame: Painless scrotal mass with mild discomfort during exercise
salient_findings: Painless, round, hazelnut-sized mass localized to the tail of the right epididymis
Solid, well-demarcated, hyperechoic, hypoperfused mass on scrotal ultrasonography
key_facts: 16-year-old male with no prior medical history
Noted a small lump in his right hemiscrotum two months earlier
Denies any history of scrotal trauma or inflammation
Lump’s size remained unchanged over two months
Experienced mild discomfort during exercise, which resolved with rest
Painless mass on physical examination
Testicles and groin were otherwise unremarkable
Scrotal ultrasonography demonstrated a 1.3 × 1.1 cm mass at the tail of the right epididymis
Mass contained two small hypoechoic foci
Routine blood tests, coagulation profile, and serum tumor markers were all within normal limits

Solid, well-demarcated, hyperechoic, hypoperfused mass on scrotal ultrasonography

Denies any history of scrotal trauma or inflammation

differentials: Malignant fibrous histiocytoma of the epididymis
Malignant fibrous histiocytoma of the epididymis

shortlist.label: Adenomatoid tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Most common epididymal tumor, matches clinical presentation of a painless, solid mass

shortlist.label: Epididymal cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Common benign condition, could present as a painless mass, although typically fluid-filled

shortlist.label: Spermatocele
shortlist.why_kept: Benign cystic structure, often near the epididymis, could cause mild discomfort

shortlist.label: Epididymal lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Benign tumor, could present as a solid, painless mass, although less common than adenomatoid tumor

shortlist.label: Papillary cystadenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare, benign tumor, could present similarly to adenomatoid tumor, but less common

raw.rationale: The presence of a solid, well-demarcated, hyperechoic mass at the tail of the epididymis with two small hypoechoic foci, as seen on scrotal ultrasonography, is consistent with an adenomatoid tumor, which is a common benign tumor of the epididymis.

rejected.label: Epididymal cyst
rejected.why: Epididymal cysts are typically fluid-filled and anechoic on ultrasonography, which does not match the solid, hyperechoic mass described in the case.

rejected.label: Spermatocele
rejected.why: Spermatoceles are cystic structures that contain sperm and are typically located at the head of the epididymis, which does not match the location or solid nature of the mass in the case.

rejected.label: Epididymal lipoma
rejected.why: Epididymal lipomas are rare and would likely appear as a hyperechoic mass on ultrasonography, but the presence of two small hypoechoic foci within the mass is not typical for a lipoma.

rejected.label: Papillary cystadenoma
rejected.why: Papillary cystadenomas are rare tumors that are typically associated with von Hippel-Lindau disease and would not be expected in a 16-year-old male with no prior medical history.
